record.paper_title: Open problems, questions and challenges in finite-dimensional integrable systems
record.original_question: Describe the structure of singularities of Phi = ( σ1,..., σn): M → Rn in terms of the singular points of the recursion operator R, their linearisations, and the corresponding left-symmet ric algebras. What are sufficient and/or necessary conditions fo r such singularities to be non-degenerate (in the sense of Eliasson [72])? Notice that, in this case, th e algebraic type of R is rather special: at a generic point, R is semisimple, but each of its eigenvalues has multiplicity 2.

What are sufficient and/or necessary conditions fo r such singularities to be non-degenerate (in the sense of Eliasson [72])? artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let (M, ω) be a smooth symplectic manifold of dimension 2n equipped with a Nijenhuis recursion operator R: TM → TM, that is, a (1,1)-tensor field whose Nijenhuis torsion vanishes and which is compatible with ω in the sense required to generate a bi-Hamiltonian (or, more generally, Nijenhuis-Hamiltonian) integrable system. Let σ_1, …, σ_n denote the elementary symmetric functions of the (generically) eigenvalues of R, and assume that {σ_i, σ_j} = 0 for all i, j with respect to the Poisson bracket induced by ω, so that the map

    Φ = (σ_1, …, σ_n): M → R^n

is the momentum map of a completely integrable Hamiltonian system. Assume that at a generic point of M the operator R is semisimple and that each of its eigenvalues has algebraic multiplicity exactly 2.

A singular point p ∈ M of Φ is said to be non-degenerate in the sense of Eliasson if, denoting by k the rank of dΦ(p), the linearised system of the components of Φ that vanish to first order at p generates a Cartan subalgebra of the Lie algebra sp(2(n−k), R) of quadratic Hamiltonians on the symplectic transverse to the orbit through p.

At a singular point p of Φ one may consider:
  (i) p as a singular point of the recursion operator R (where the spectral or Jordan type of R degenerates),
  (ii) the linearisation of R at p,
  (iii) the left-symmetric algebra structure naturally attached to R at p (the algebra whose product is determined by the linearisation of R viewed as an endomorphism on the tangent space).

Problem.
(a) Describe the structure of the singularities of Φ in terms of the data (i)–(iii) above; i.e. give an explicit correspondence between the local geometry of the critical set of Φ and the singular behaviour of R together with its linearisation and associated left-symmetric algebra.
(b) Find sufficient conditions, expressed purely in terms of (i)–(iii), under which a singular point of Φ is non-degenerate in the sense of Eliasson.
(c) Find necessary conditions of the same kind, and ideally a combined necessary-and-sufficient criterion.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted search did not reveal a published full resolution of this problem on singularities of integrable systems generated by a Nijenhuis recursion operator with double eigenvalues. The problem is stated as an open problem in the integrable-systems literature, and recent works on Nijenhuis geometry and bi-Hamiltonian singularities address related but more restricted settings (simple eigenvalues, or specific normal forms), without providing the requested general structural correspondence with left-symmetric algebras and Eliasson non-degeneracy.

status_evidence.title: Open problems, questions and challenges in finite-dimensional integrable systems
status_evidence.snippet: Problem 5.17 lists the description of singularities of Φ in terms of R, its linearisation and associated left-symmetric algebras, and the search for non-degeneracy criteria à la Eliasson, as an open problem.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is posed as an open problem in a list of open problems in finite-dimensional integrable systems.
